title: L1 Data Cache Access Method
decision: Cycle the L1 data cache array at twice the core processor clock frequency to provide two load/store accesses per cycle.
alternatives_or_rejected: Building a true multi-ported SRAM or using complex banking with conflict resolution logic.
rationale: Multi-ported SRAMs consume excessive die area and have slower access times; banking introduces stalls. Double-pumping trades clocking complexity for area and speed.
outcome: The data cache effectively operates at double frequency, supporting the high-bandwidth out-of-order engine without the area penalty of multi-porting.

title: Issue Queue Organization
decision: Implement physically separate, distributed issue queues for Integer and Floating-Point instructions.
alternatives_or_rejected: A single, large centralized unified issue queue or reservation station.
rationale: A single large queue would have wire-delay and access-time penalties that limit maximum clock frequency. Separating them keeps arrays smaller, faster, and closer to execution units.
outcome: Enabled higher clock frequencies and reduced issue latency, though it required duplicating some control logic.

title: Tournament Branch Predictor
decision: Implement a tournament branch predictor that dynamically selects between a local-history predictor and a global-history predictor for each branch.
alternatives_or_rejected: A simple gshare predictor, a pure bimodal predictor, or a single global-history table.
rationale: Different branches exhibit different correlation behaviors; some correlate strongly with their own local history, while others correlate with the global execution path. A tournament predictor adapts to both without the aliasing problems of forcing all branches into one history scheme.
outcome: High branch prediction accuracy that was critical for the deep pipeline and high clock frequency of the 21264.
